thread:
Morgan: quick heads-up — noticed a checked-in aws access key in feature/ux-avatars while reviewing a PR. not used in prod but present in history. 
Akash: ouch. which repo? can you paste the blob or a git sha?
Morgan: repo: infra-utils, commit: b4f3c9a. here is the grep line: `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=AKIA...xyz`
Noah: thanks for flagging. first step: rotate key and revoke any sessions. @rotation-bot can you schedule rotation for the IAM user? we should assume credentials leaked.
rotation-bot: @Noah noted. Scheduling automatic rotation for IAM user `svc-ci-builder` in 15m and creating ticket RED-4597. Will post when done. :gear:
Sara: Also check Vault - if that key was ever put into Vault transit or KV, we need to rotate the Vault version and audit logs. Did anyone see the key in vault kv v2?
Morgan: I searched vault kv namespaces: nothing obvious, but I haven't checked archived snapshots. ran `vault kv get -version=2 secret/infra/ci` — no matching entry in current versions.
Akash: good. Still, we need to ensure audit logs show any reads. Security Oncall, can you pull the Vault audit trail between the commit time and now? specifically reads to secret/infra/ci and any token auths for svc-ci-builder.
Security Oncall: on it. I triggered a query against splunk: `index=vault_logs action=read user="svc-ci-builder" OR path="secret/infra/*" earliest=-24h`. Pulling results now.
Noah: we should also update RBAC so that CI service accounts can't create long-lived keys. Put a policy that denies iam:CreateAccessKey except for a short list. Akash, can infra patch org-policy?
Akash: yeah planning a change. Proposal: deny CreateAccessKey by default, allow only assumed-role for automation that issues ephemeral creds. I'll open infra PR and pin to canary.
Morgan: timeline? we should lock this down before any new rotations to avoid churn.
Akash: PR in ~45m, hoping for quick review. will add a feature flag to flip for prod accounts only first.
Security Oncall: Splunk shows 3 reads from the host that triggered the commit, but all reads appear to be from the dev workstation user, not from CI. No vault auth from svc-ci-builder in the window. I've attached the search result snippet: ```user: "morgan.workstation", path: "*feature/ux-avatars*", action: read```
Sara: ok good — that reduces blast radius. Still treat it as secret exposure. Next: rotate AWS key, revoke existing sessions, rotate any dependent API tokens that used that key, and update any build configs that referenced it. Morgan — can you scan repos for accidental references to the same key pattern? use `git log -S"AKIA" --all` and `git grep "AKIA"`.
Morgan: running scan now. found one more hit in a forked branch on the same repo. cleaning it.
Noah: add audit logging for KMS usage on the key that encrypted CI blobs. If the key was used to encrypt anything, we need to re-encrypt with a fresh CMK. @vault-bot, can you confirm which KMS CMK is used for `secret/infra/ci`?
vault-bot: Vault secret `secret/infra/ci` uses KMS key arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Last rotated 2024-11-03.
Akash: file a quick ticket to rotate that CMK and schedule re-encryption for any objects encrypted with that key. For objects in S3, we can do S3 Copy+Replace with new key; for EBS snapshots we may need snapshot copy.
Security Oncall: created ticket RED-4598 for CMK rotation and re-encryption. Setting priority P1 given potential credential exposure.
Sara: also update audit retention — keep KMS and Vault audit logs for 90 days for this incident at least. We should enable object-level logging if not already on.
Noah: who will own the rotations? Morgan to confirm repos cleaned, Akash to deploy RBAC deny rule and rotate CMK, Security Oncall to revoke IAM keys and run audit queries. I'll coordinate any customer notifications if there are external exposures.
Morgan: I finished cleaning forks and opened PR to remove the blob from history (git filter-repo) and posted the rewrite to the infra repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-utils/pull/612
Akash: rotation-bot reports IAM access key for svc-ci-builder revoked at 1758123780. Please verify builds that depend on that user fail and we can patch credentials into the new short-lived role.
Sara: remember to update the Redwood Console entries for any service that used the old key (secrets mapping). Otherwise infra health checks will keep failing silently.
Security Oncall: final note — document timeline and evidence in the incident Red-4597 thread, mark as confidential, and run postmortem once stable. For now, keep channel limited to relevant folks. :lock:
Noah: thanks everyone. if anything else pops up tag @Security Oncall. I'll follow up with remediation checklist and handoff.
